thread:
Sarah (PM): Quick sync — I pulled together the top field asks for private deployments next quarter. Shortlist: preserve customer egress IPs, minimal/offline installer footprint, and customer-managed KMS/HSM. Need to decide priorities and launch gates.
Ryan (NetOps): Preserving egress IPs is the heavy one. Options are relay/proxy (easy) vs BGP/peering or SNAT on host (hard). Customers that need it are large finance/healthcare.
Jess (Field): +1 on prioritizing egress IP for two active deals. They literally have policies that block any new NAT pool. If we can promise preservation it's a deal win.
Mike (Eng): From an implementation POV we can do phased approach: Phase A = relay/egress-proxy with IP mapping for small customers. Phase B = operator shim that manages host routing / BGP for enterprise. Phase C = on-prem hardware BGP integration. Can we scope a tech spike for Phase B?
Anya (Runtime): Important perf note: hostNetwork/BGP paths force us to handle KV cache locality differently and will break some autoscaling assumptions. Also installer size: shipping BGP tooling + binaries increases bundle by ~40MB.
Sarah (PM): Good details. What would we need to call the feature "GA"? Suggested launch criteria: 1) E2E test preserving customer IPs for a sample 3 topologies, 2) installer <200MB for airgapped option, 3) KMS integration tested with at-rest and in-use rotations, 4) rollback path validated (<15m). Thoughts?
Ryan (NetOps): Agree on criteria. Add: documented network preflight checks and automated validation (IP-preserve smoke test). Also require a fallback mode that routes through Redwood relay if BGP peering fails.
Jess (Field): Also require sales-facing packaging: clear tiering (basic = relay, enterprise = IP-preserve + dedicated support). Customers want SLAs on egress determinism.
Mike (Eng): For the tech spike: estimate 2-3 sprints to prototype operator shim + smoke tests. After spike we can estimate full work. Note: operator shim will need privileged node hooks — security review required.
Anya (Runtime): KMS/HSM: we'll need to add support for customer KMS endpoints and test with offline installer. HSM brings ingress/outbound constraints (network policy to HSM endpoints). Might be separate deliverable but must be on roadmap.
Sarah (PM): Prioritization proposal: 1) Phase B tech spike (operator shim) immediate, 2) airgap/minimal-installer improvements in parallel, 3) KMS/HSM integration scoped as milestone after spike. Launch gate = successful enterprise canary + field signoff.
Ryan (NetOps): +1. If we run the spike, we should include a test plan: BGP peering simulated, host SNAT toggle, ip-preserve smoke. I'll draft.
Mike (Eng): I'll own the spike and draft a PRD with acceptance tests. Need @Anya to review runtime implications.
Anya (Runtime): Happy to review. Also flag: telemetry — some customers demand minimal telemetry by default in private mode; we'll add a setting and an acceptance test to ensure no accidental outbound calls.
Jess (Field): I'll align with the two priority customers and get their acceptance criteria in writing. Means we can validate the rollout.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: private-spike-env -> staging at 4176543290 :rocket:
Sarah (PM): Action items: Mike -> PRD + spike plan by EOD Wed; Ryan -> test plan draft; Jess -> collect customer acceptance docs; Anya -> runtime checklist (autoscale, telemetry, installer size). We'll reconvene next Wed. :calendar:
Mike (Eng): Sounds good. I'll post the PRD draft in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
Jess (Field): Thanks — if we can get the egress story nailed down, it unlocks 2 big deals.
Sarah (PM): Great, closing loop here. Keeping scope tight for initial rollout helps.
